After Young's inequality and Gronwall, the Gronwall constant necessarily depends on these additional quantities, so the bound is not uniform in the class $\bmf{\Phi}\in\bmf{X}$ as stated.

issues.title: Constant C in Lemma lem-m-H2 understates its dependence on $\bmf{\Phi}$

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma lem-con proves only that consecutive differences $\|\tilde{\bmf{m}}^{l+1}-\tilde{\bmf{m}}^l\|_{\bmf{H}^2}\to0$ (Cauchy convergence), not that $\tilde{\bmf{m}}^l\to\bmf{m}$ (convergence to the LL solution). Passing to the limit in the iteration to show the limit solves the LL equation and invoking uniqueness is missing. The claim $\|\bmf{m}_h-\tilde{\bmf{m}}_h^l\|\to0$ (discrete fixed-point convergence) is asserted without any proof or analogue of Lemma lem-con for the discrete scheme. Additionally, Proposition pro2 assumes initialisation $\tilde{\bmf{m}}_h^0=R_h\tilde{\bmf{m}}_0$ while Theorem thm-error states $\bmf{m}_h^0=I_h\bmf{m}_0$, so $\|\bmf{m}_h-\tilde{\bmf{m}}_h^l\|$ cannot tend to zero with different initial data.

issues.failure_explanation: For a continuous piecewise-linear vector function $\bmf{m}_h\in\bmf{S}_h$, requiring $|\bmf{m}_h(\bmf{x})|=1$ at every point forces the affine restriction $A_K\bmf{x}+\bmf{b}_K$ on each element to satisfy $A_K^TA_K=0$, hence $A_K=0$ and $\bmf{m}_h$ is globally constant with unit norm. The proposition then states energy dissipation only for constant (equilibrium) solutions, where the conclusion is trivially true and has no dynamical content. No nontrivial evolution in $\bmf{S}_h$ can satisfy the hypothesis, so the advertised energy dissipation law for the FVEM dynamics is vacuous. The failure mechanism is an incompatible hypothesis that eliminates every nontrivial case; none of the three standard categories applies cleanly.

failure_location.quote: the discrete magnetization $\bmf{m}_h$ satisfies $|\bmf{m}_h| = 1$ in a point-wise sense

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the constraint to node-wise unit norm ($|\bmf{m}_h(\bmf{x}_i)|=1$ at mesh nodes, matching the GSPM projection step) or to an $L^2$-type constraint, and supply a proof under the weakened hypothesis (which necessarily also requires repairing the proof errors catalogued in ISSUE-006).
issues.overall_effect: The discrete energy dissipation law — a headline guarantee of the paper's Section 3.3 — holds only for constant magnetisation and provides no validation of energy decay for actual dynamics.
issues.title: Pointwise unit-norm assumption on $\bmf{m}_h\in\bmf{S}_h$ forces $\bmf{m}_h$ to be constant, vacuating Proposition energy-dissipation
issues.why_classification: No comparable version of the energy-dissipation guarantee survives the stated hypothesis: the result is vacuous for every nontrivial numerical solution, and any weakening immediately triggers additional proof failures that require a substantially different argument.

issues.failure_explanation: Three invalid steps combine: (1) The proof sets $(\bmf{m}_h\times\partial_t\bmf{m}_h,\,I_h^*\partial_t\bmf{m}_h)=0$ by invoking $\bmf{m}_h\cdot\partial_t\bmf{m}_h=0$, but $(\bmf{a}\times\bmf{b})\cdot\bmf{c}=0$ requires $\bmf{c}=\bmf{b}$; since $I_h^*\partial_t\bmf{m}_h\neq\partial_t\bmf{m}_h$ the integrand does not vanish. (2) The terms $\epsilon(|\nabla\bmf{m}_h|^2\bmf{m}_h,\,I_h^*\partial_t\bmf{m}_h)$ and $(\bmf{m}_h\cdot\hat{\bmf{f}})(\bmf{m}_h,\,I_h^*\partial_t\bmf{m}_h)$ are dropped using $\bmf{m}_h\cdot I_h^*\partial_t\bmf{m}_h=0$, which also fails. (3) The energy derivative is written as $\epsilon\,d_t|||\bmf{m}_h|||_h^2-(\hat{\bmf{f}},I_h^*\partial_t\bmf{m}_h)$, but differentiating $F=\tfrac{\epsilon}{2}|||\bmf{m}_h|||_h^2+(\hat{F},1)$ gives $\tfrac{\epsilon}{2}\,d_t|||\bmf{m}_h|||_h^2-(\hat{\bmf{f}},\partial_t\bmf{m}_h)$ — a factor-of-two error and a spurious $I_h^*$. These errors cause the key cancellations in the proof to fail, leaving unclosed $O(1)$ terms.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace every use of $I_h^*\partial_t\bmf{m}_h$ in the energy derivative by $\partial_t\bmf{m}_h$ (using the correct formula $\tfrac{\epsilon}{2}d_t|||\bmf{m}_h|||^2_h-(\hat{\bmf{f}},\partial_t\bmf{m}_h)$), and supply a new argument to control the residual terms involving $\bmf{m}_h\cdot I_h^*\partial_t\bmf{m}_h$ and $(\bmf{m}_h\times\partial_t\bmf{m}_h,I_h^*\partial_t\bmf{m}_h)$ — either by bounding them with inverse/consistency estimates and absorbing them into the dissipation, or by reformulating the discrete energy identity in the dual-mesh inner product throughout.
issues.overall_effect: The discrete energy dissipation law $d_tF[\bmf{m}_h]\leq 0$ is not proved for any nontrivial numerical solution; the derivation of the energy inequality rests on false orthogonality identities and an incorrect differentiation formula.
issues.title: Energy-dissipation proof treats $I_h^*\partial_t\bmf{m}_h$ as $\partial_t\bmf{m}_h$ and uses an incorrect energy-derivative formula
issues.why_classification: The repair requires a contained nontrivial argument to handle the $I_h^*$ interpolation error in the energy identity, plus a local formula correction; no global proof architecture change or guarantee weakening is needed once the constraint hypothesis is appropriately interpreted.
